r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Fifth mutation defeats the universal runtime pin while it stays fully green. Mutated spine_status in call_tool so an undeclared key named spine_path (one of the generator's own adversarial keys, marker spine crossed with affix _path) makes the handler read a decoy spine file directly and return its content, never calling run_engine or checklist_engine.main at all. Ran IdentityBindingPinTests: 7 passed, including the universal pin test. Mechanism: that test patches checklist_engine.main and asserts only inside a loop over the captured argv list; when a handler answers without reaching run_engine, the capture list stays empty and the loop body never executes, so nothing is checked for that tool/key pair -- a redirect that never touches the engine is invisible to a pin that only inspects what reached the engine. Independently confirmed the redirect is live outside the suite: drove call_tool directly against a bound spine marked PIN-MARK and a decoy marked DECOY-MARK; response text was PEEK: MARKER::DECOY-MARK, never the bound content. Restored the door via git checkout; diff empty, file byte-identical to a pre-mutation backup, suite back to 7 passed. This is the exact shape the task named in advance: a redirect that never touches --file but reaches another spine some other way.

consolidation.summary: The second reviewer's exact finding (target_spine enumeration gap) is genuinely resolved: reproduced RED on test_no_argument_can_change_the_identity_the_engine_is_addressed_with. But the universal runtime pin has a structural gap of its own -- it only inspects argv actually captured from checklist_engine.main, so a handler that answers a call without ever reaching run_engine escapes it entirely. Demonstrated live: an undeclared spine_path key on spine_status made the handler read a decoy spine directly and return its content (confirmed via PEEK: MARKER::DECOY-MARK outside the suite), with all 7 pin tests staying green. Restored and reproducible. Triage candidate tc1 filed for widening the pin or routing every call_tool path through run_engine provably.

triage_candidates.statement: The MCP door confinement pin (tests/test_mcp_identity.py::IdentityBindingPinTests::test_no_argument_can_change_the_identity_the_engine_is_addressed_with) only inspects argv actually captured from checklist_engine.main; a call_tool handler that answers a call without ever reaching run_engine escapes the pin entirely regardless of key name, demonstrated live via an undeclared spine_path key on spine_status that reads and returns a decoy spine's content directly. Widen the pin so a handler that never calls checklist_engine.main is itself treated as a violation (or wrap call_tool so every code path is provably routed through run_engine before it can return content), and narrow IDENTITY_TRADE.md section 2's claim to name what is actually decidable in the meantime.
